author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Turn on logging in a Cloud DNS server policy (or on a public zone), and route the entries with a Log Router sink filtered on resource.type="dns_query" to a Pub/Sub topic. A push subscription can't send the Authorization header HTTP Ingest needs, so the example bridge in bridges/google-cloud-pubsub pulls them and posts each entry to HTTP Ingest unchanged. Sophos Fusion's Google Cloud Platform integration reads a Pub/Sub subscription too, but its docs list audit logs, Security Command Center findings and flow logs only; whether it hands Cloud DNS entries to custom parsers hasn't been checked. Every query goes to the DNS schema: the name without its trailing dot and in lower case, the type and response code as numbers, the client as the source address, the forwarding target as the destination address, the VM's instance ID as host_id, and the first four answers, from structuredRdata or, failing that, from rdata, which Cloud DNS cuts off at 260 bytes. The DNS schema has no field for the project, network, VM name, protocol, target type (such as a private zone, a forwarding zone or a response policy), latency or egress error, so they stay in original_data. Reverse lookups get no top private domain. Samples follow the field table in Google's Cloud DNS logging docs and the entries in Google's Apache-2.0 samples, with made-up values; structuredRdata appears only in Google Security Operations' parser docs, so it is unconfirmed. Passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-22 (79 of 79 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and no built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.
